_purpose: Executable test cases (EC) for UC1a — runnable expansion of the scenarios. Per scenario: 1 success EC + exactly one alternative EC per expected.alternative[] entry.
_status: phase-3-4 output — 2026-07-09. Derived from PDT-3562-uc1a-scenarios.json (12 SC / 11 AC). UC1a = the video / recorded-LS player component (surface token = 'Video player'). SC-UC1a-05 alt[1] (recorded-LS exact-resume) is observe/record — held under pending FU ASSUME-recorded-resume; its success (video exact-resume) and alt[0] (Live-edge contrast) are assertable now.
_id_note: EC- = Executable Case. Chain: AC → SC → EC. (TC- = L3 condition; SC- = scenario.)

cases.name: [Video player] Verify first tap reveals controls without toggling playback (mobile, playing)
preconditions: a video / recorded LS is playing on a mobile surface (iOS)
the controls overlay is hidden
currentTime is advancing (position 0:30)
steps: Tap anywhere on the player surface (first tap) at position 0:30
Assert: the controls overlay is visible
Assert: playback continues — currentTime keeps advancing past 0:30 and video.paused is false
Assert: the central button icon is PAUSE
cases.expected_result: On mobile, the first tap on a playing video/recorded LS reveals the controls overlay while playback continues uninterrupted (currentTime keeps advancing, video.paused===false) and the central button shows the PAUSE icon — the tap does not toggle playback.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify first tap never pauses the media (mobile accidental-interrupt guard)
preconditions: a video / recorded LS is playing on a mobile surface (iOS)
the controls overlay is hidden
position 0:30
steps: Tap anywhere on the player surface (first tap) at position 0:30
Assert: video.paused is false — currentTime keeps advancing, the tap did NOT pause
Assert: the central button icon is PAUSE, not PLAY (a PLAY icon would be the desktop 1-Step-Pause class)
cases.expected_result: On mobile, a first tap that PAUSES the media (currentTime stops / play icon shows) is the wrong class — that is the desktop 1-Step-Pause behaviour (BR-09); on mobile a reveal that toggles playback is the accidental-interrupt regression this story exists to prevent (BR-10).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify first tap is never a no-op (overlay must appear)
preconditions: a video / recorded LS is playing on a mobile surface (iOS)
the controls overlay is hidden
position 0:30
steps: Tap anywhere on the player surface (first tap) at position 0:30
Assert: the controls overlay is visible — the tap was not swallowed as a no-op
Assert: playback also did not pause (video.paused is false)
cases.expected_result: The overlay must actually appear — a first tap that neither reveals the controls nor pauses (a no-op) is a failure.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify tap outside the central button dismisses the overlay and playback continues
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
the central button's rendered hit-target is 64x64px (FU-2 resolved)
steps: Tap the player surface OUTSIDE the central button's 64x64px tap target
Assert: the overlay is dismissed (no longer visible)
Assert: video.paused is false — playback continues uninterrupted, state stays playing
cases.expected_result: Tapping outside the 64x64px central button dismisses the overlay while playback continues uninterrupted (state stays playing) — the dismiss is not an implicit pause.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify a tap just inside the 64x64px central button pauses instead of dismissing (boundary)
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
the central button's rendered hit-target is 64x64px (FU-2 resolved)
steps: Tap just INSIDE the rendered 64x64px central button
Assert: video.paused becomes true (state transitions playing -> paused) — this is a pause, not a dismiss
Assert: the overlay is NOT dismissed by this tap
cases.expected_result: A tap just INSIDE the rendered 64x64px central button pauses (playing -> paused) instead of dismissing — the pause-vs-dismiss boundary (FU-2 resolved: 64x64px; assert against the rendered target, which may be native).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify tap-outside never implicitly pauses the media
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
the central button's rendered hit-target is 64x64px (FU-2 resolved)
steps: Tap the player surface OUTSIDE the 64x64px central button
Assert: video.paused stays false — the tap-outside did NOT transition playing -> paused
cases.expected_result: A tap-outside that transitions playing -> paused is a failure — dismissing the overlay must never implicitly pause the media (BR-10).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify overlay auto-dismisses after 1s of no action (playing)
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
no further user interaction occurs
steps: Reveal the overlay while playing, then take no action
Advance the idle timer to 900ms; Assert: the overlay is still visible
Advance the idle timer to 1000ms; Assert: the overlay is auto-dismissed
Assert: playback continues throughout — currentTime is still advancing
cases.expected_result: After exactly 1s (1000ms) of no interaction while playing, the overlay auto-dismisses and playback continues (currentTime still advancing); at 900ms it is still visible.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify overlay still visible at 900ms (never dismisses before 1s)
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
no further user interaction occurs
steps: Reveal the overlay while playing, take no action
Advance the idle timer to 900ms
Assert: the overlay is still visible at 900ms (not dismissed before the 1s bound)
cases.expected_result: At 900ms (just below the 1s bound) the overlay must still be visible — dismissing before 1s is a boundary failure.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify overlay dismisses at 1000ms not 3000ms (web 3s->1s regression guard)
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
no further user interaction occurs
steps: Reveal the overlay while playing, take no action
Advance the idle timer to 1000ms
Assert: the overlay is dismissed at 1000ms — not held until 3000ms (VideoPlayerControls.tsx:60-70)
cases.expected_result: The overlay must auto-dismiss at 1000ms, not 3000ms — web currently uses a 3s timer (VideoPlayerControls.tsx:60-70); any dismiss later than 1s fails the regression guard (iOS is already 1s).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify pause shows play icon + seek controls, paused overlay persists, tap-outside stays paused
preconditions: a video / recorded LS is playing with the controls overlay visible
the central button's rendered hit-target is 64x64px (FU-2 resolved)
steps: Tap the central pause button
Assert: video.paused is true — paused at the current position
Assert: the icon switched pause -> play and the PLAY icon remains visible
Assert: BOTH the -10s AND the +10s skip buttons remain visible (video/recorded component — BR-01)
Advance >1000ms (to 1500ms) with no interaction; Assert: the overlay persists (the paused branch has no idle auto-dismiss)
Tap outside the 64x64px central button; Assert: the overlay is dismissed AND video.paused is still true (the media did not resume)
cases.expected_result: On a playing video/recorded LS the central pause tap pauses playback at the current position and the play icon persists; the +/-10s seek controls remain visible; while paused the overlay persists past 1s (no idle auto-dismiss); a tap-outside dismisses the overlay and the media stays paused.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify an active Live stream shows no +/-10s seek controls (contrast)
preconditions: an active Live stream is playing with the controls overlay visible
SDK stream type mocked = Live
steps: Mock: SDK stream type = Live
Reveal the overlay and tap the central pause button
Assert: neither the -10s nor the +10s skip button is rendered (seek is gated to video/recorded)
cases.expected_result: Contrast: on an active Live stream the +/-10s seek controls are NOT shown — proving the seek gate is stream-type driven; seek exists only on video/recorded (BR-01, TC-UC1a-01c).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify a paused overlay never auto-dismisses on the 1s idle timer
preconditions: a video / recorded LS is paused with the controls overlay (play icon) visible
no further user interaction occurs
steps: Pause the media so the overlay shows the PLAY icon
Advance >1000ms (to 1500ms) with no interaction
Assert: the overlay still persists — the paused branch has no idle timeout (does not auto-dismiss at 1s)
cases.expected_result: A paused overlay must NOT auto-dismiss on the 1s idle timer — the paused branch has no idle timeout, so it persists until a tap-outside (BR-11).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify tap-outside while paused never resumes playback
preconditions: a video / recorded LS is paused with the controls overlay visible
the central button's rendered hit-target is 64x64px (FU-2 resolved)
steps: With the media paused and the overlay visible, tap outside the 64x64px central button
Assert: the overlay is dismissed
Assert: video.paused is still true — the media did not resume (the dismiss is not an implicit play)
cases.expected_result: A tap-outside while paused must never resume playback — the dismiss is not an implicit play; the media stays paused (BR-10).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify tap play resumes a paused video from the exact position (0:42)
preconditions: a video is paused at a known position (t=42s) on a known-length local fixture
the central play button is displayed
steps: With the video paused at 0:42, tap the central play button
Assert: playback resumes from currentTime === 0:42 (not 0:00, not the live edge)
Assert: the icon switched play -> pause
cases.expected_result: Tapping the central play button on a paused video resumes playback from the exact paused position (t=42s -> resumes at 42s, not 0 and not the live edge); the icon switches play -> pause.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify resume on a Live stream jumps to the live edge (not the paused position)
preconditions: a Live stream is paused at t=42s
SDK stream type mocked = Live
steps: Mock: SDK stream type = Live, paused at 0:42
Tap the central play button
Assert: playback resumes at the current live edge (approx. live within the CONF-07 tolerance), NOT 0:42
cases.expected_result: On a Live stream, resume goes to the current live edge (approx. live within tolerance), NOT the exact paused position — a media-type contrast (BR-13; cross-ref UC2 CONF-07 tolerance).

cases.name: [Video player] Observe recorded-LS resume position (ASSUME-recorded-resume — do NOT assert)
preconditions: a recorded LS is paused at t=42s
SDK stream type mocked = recorded LS
steps: Mock: SDK stream type = recorded LS, paused at 0:42
Tap the central play button
Observe and record the resume position (screenshot + notes): does it resume at 0:42 like video, or snap to the live edge?
cases.expected_result: OBSERVE/RECORD ONLY — recorded LS is assumed to resume from the exact paused position (0:42) like video, but this is unconfirmed; do NOT assert until Engineering closes ASSUME-recorded-resume (TC-UC1a-07b). Record whether recorded LS resumes at 0:42 or snaps to the live edge.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify reveal / dismiss / pause / resume behaviour is identical across all 6 in-scope surfaces
preconditions: a video / recorded LS renders on an in-scope surface
the platform (form factor) is held fixed while the surface varies
steps: For each of the 6 surfaces {global feed, user feed, community feed, event-discussion feed, media gallery, fullscreen}: perform reveal, tap-outside dismiss, 1s auto-dismiss, pause, resume; record the outcomes
Assert: on every surface the outcomes are identical — the overlay reveals and playback continues the same way (surface-invariant)
cases.expected_result: The reveal / tap-outside-dismiss / 1s auto-dismiss / pause / resume behaviours produce identical outcomes across all 6 in-scope surfaces {global, user, community, event-discussion feed, media gallery, fullscreen} (surface-invariant).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify no in-scope surface diverges from another (surface-invariance break)
preconditions: a video / recorded LS renders on an in-scope surface
the platform (form factor) is held fixed while the surface varies
steps: Run the reveal / dismiss / auto-dismiss / pause / resume flow on all 6 in-scope surfaces with the platform held fixed
Compare the outcomes pairwise across surfaces
Assert: no surface produces a different outcome than another in-scope surface (any divergence is a BR-06 surface-invariance break)
cases.expected_result: Any in-scope surface producing a DIFFERENT reveal / dismiss / auto-dismiss / pause / resume outcome than another in-scope surface is a surface-invariance break (BR-06 violation).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify no controls overlay before the first tap (default state)
preconditions: a video / recorded LS is actively playing on an in-scope surface
the post has just rendered
no tap has occurred yet
steps: Render the actively-playing post without any tap
Assert: no controls overlay element exists in the view hierarchy / DOM
Assert: only the media surface is visible
cases.expected_result: On first render of an actively-playing video/recorded LS on any in-scope surface, with no tap yet, no controls overlay element exists in the view hierarchy / DOM — only the media surface is visible (baseline default state).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify the overlay is never present pre-interaction (baseline default-state guard)
preconditions: a video / recorded LS is actively playing on an in-scope surface
no tap has occurred yet
steps: Render the actively-playing post with no tap
Assert: no controls-overlay element is present in the view hierarchy / DOM before any tap
cases.expected_result: The controls overlay must NOT be present before any tap — an overlay element rendered pre-interaction is a baseline default-state failure.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify a control interaction resets the 1s idle countdown
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
the 1s idle countdown is running
steps: With the overlay visible over playing media and the 1s countdown running, interact with the scrubber at 800ms
Assert: the countdown restarts — the overlay is still visible past the original 1000ms
Take no further action; Assert: the overlay auto-dismisses 1000ms after the LAST interaction
Assert: playback continues throughout
cases.expected_result: A control interaction at 800ms restarts the 1s idle countdown — the overlay stays visible through the interaction and auto-dismisses only 1000ms after the LAST interaction; playback continues throughout.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify the countdown never ignores a later interaction (must not dismiss on first reveal)
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
the 1s idle countdown is running
steps: Reveal the overlay, then interact with a control (scrubber) at 800ms
Advance the clock to 1000ms after the FIRST reveal
Assert: the overlay is still visible — the timer restarted on the interaction and did NOT dismiss 1000ms after the first reveal
cases.expected_result: If the overlay dismisses 1000ms after the FIRST reveal — ignoring the later interaction — the countdown-reset failed; the timer must restart on every control interaction, so repeated interactions each less than 1s apart never dismiss the overlay while the user is still interacting (TC-UC1a-02d).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify pause tap wins the race against the auto-dismiss timer
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
the 1s idle auto-dismiss timer is about to fire (t approx 999ms)
steps: Dispatch a central pause-button tap at ~999ms — the instant the auto-dismiss would fire (fake-timer race)
Assert: the explicit pause WINS — video.paused becomes true
Assert: the PLAY icon is shown and persists (not swallowed by the expiring timer)
Assert: the overlay dismisses only on a subsequent tap-outside, not from the fired timer
cases.expected_result: When the central pause tap lands at ~999ms as the 1s auto-dismiss is about to fire, the explicit pause wins: the media pauses, the play icon shows and persists (not swallowed by the expiring timer), and the overlay dismisses only on a subsequent tap-outside.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify the expiring 1s timer never swallows the pause
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
the 1s idle auto-dismiss timer is about to fire (t approx 999ms)
steps: Dispatch the central pause tap at ~999ms as the 1s timer fires (fake-timer race)
Assert: the overlay does NOT auto-dismiss discarding the pause — the paused / play-icon state is retained (video.paused is true) and the media does not stay playing
cases.expected_result: The expiring 1s timer must not swallow the pause — a race where the overlay auto-dismisses and the paused / play-icon state is lost (or the media stays playing) is the failure mode; a PLAYING overlay would have dismissed on the timer, but once paused the overlay persists (dismisses only via tap-outside).

cases.name: [Video player] Verify tap during buffering reveals the real state, never a false playing icon
preconditions: the media is buffering (not yet playing)
buffering is forced via network throttle / route delay or a state mock
steps: Force buffering via network throttle / route delay, then tap the player surface
Assert: the controls overlay is visible
Assert: the central button reflects the REAL state (loading/paused) — NOT a false 'playing' pause-icon
Assert: no crash and no frozen overlay
Release the throttle; Assert: once playback starts the icon updates to the playing state
cases.expected_result: Tapping the player surface while buffering reveals the overlay with the central button reflecting the real state (loading/paused) — never a false 'playing' pause-icon — with no crash and no frozen overlay; once playback starts the icon updates to the playing state.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify a mid-playback stall surfaces a loading state (never a silent frozen frame)
preconditions: the media was playing, then the network stalls mid-playback
the stall is injected via network manipulation (mock preferred — flake risk)
steps: Start playback, then inject a mid-playback network stall (mock preferred — flake risk)
Assert: an explicit loading/stall state is surfaced — the viewer is not left on a silent frozen frame (BR-15)
cases.expected_result: [AI-INFERRED] A mid-playback stall (was playing, then the network stalls) must surface an explicit loading/stall state — the viewer is never left on a silent frozen frame (BR-15). Extends AC-10's initial-buffer case to a mid-play stall per BR-15 'any interruption' (TC-UC1a-08c); inject via network manipulation — flake risk, mock preferred.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify the central button never shows a false playing icon while buffering
preconditions: the media is buffering (not yet playing)
buffering is forced via network throttle / route delay or a state mock
steps: Force buffering, then tap the player surface
Assert: the central button never shows a 'playing' pause-icon while buffering — it reflects the real (loading/paused) state
cases.expected_result: The central button must never show a false 'playing' pause-icon while the media is buffering — it must reflect the real (loading/paused) state.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify backgrounding while playing OS-pauses and dismisses the playing overlay on foreground
preconditions: iOS
the controls overlay is visible while the media is PLAYING
the app is backgrounded
wall-clock time > 1s passes while backgrounded
steps: Background the app with a playing overlay visible
Wait > 1s (wall clock)
Return the app to the foreground
Assert: the OS paused the media on background and does NOT auto-resume (video.paused is true)
Assert: the playing overlay is dismissed (its wall-clock 1s idle timer elapsed while backgrounded)
Assert: no stale mid-countdown overlay is shown
cases.expected_result: On returning to the foreground after backgrounding while PLAYING, the OS-paused media does not auto-resume and the playing overlay is dismissed (its wall-clock 1s idle timer elapsed while backgrounded); there is no stale mid-countdown overlay.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify the media never silently auto-resumes on foreground (playing branch)
preconditions: iOS
the controls overlay was visible while the media was PLAYING
the app was backgrounded > 1s
steps: Background while playing, wait > 1s, return the app to the foreground
Assert: video.paused stays true — no silent auto-resume (the OS pause is terminal, BR-10)
Assert: no stale mid-countdown overlay is left frozen on screen
cases.expected_result: The media must not silently auto-resume on foreground — the OS pause is a terminal action, not an implicit app toggle (BR-10); and no stale mid-countdown overlay may be left frozen on screen.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify backgrounding while paused keeps it paused and persists the paused overlay on foreground
preconditions: iOS
the controls overlay is visible while the media is PAUSED
the app is backgrounded
the user then returns the app to the foreground
steps: Background the app with a paused overlay visible
Return the app to the foreground
Assert: the media stays paused (video.paused is true; no auto-resume)
Assert: the paused overlay persists (no idle timer to elapse)
Assert: no stale mid-countdown overlay is shown
cases.expected_result: On returning to the foreground after backgrounding while PAUSED, the media stays paused (no auto-resume) and the paused overlay persists (the paused branch has no idle timer to elapse); there is no stale mid-countdown overlay.

cases.name: [Video player] Verify the paused overlay never vanishes and never auto-resumes on foreground (paused branch)
preconditions: iOS
the controls overlay was visible while the media was PAUSED
the app was backgrounded and then foregrounded
steps: Background while paused, return the app to the foreground
Assert: video.paused stays true — no auto-resume
Assert: the paused overlay is still present (did not vanish) and no stale mid-countdown overlay is shown
cases.expected_result: The media must not auto-resume and the paused overlay must not vanish on foreground — the paused branch has no idle timer and the OS pause is terminal (BR-11 + BR-10); no stale mid-countdown overlay.
